name: Emeka Usman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What is a normal working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and have just become a junior manager of the missed-collection desk for a large waste company. Six people take reports from residents and match them to a crew route. I spent years riding with collection teams and know which narrow streets need a smaller vehicle, but I am slow with staff budgets and formal reports. My bachelor’s degree did not teach me that part, and the older managers are better at it.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does your life outside work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works in a school kitchen, and our grown children have their own homes. We still have a small mortgage and about four months of expenses saved. My pay is typical for a manager here, and there are some other service offices nearby. I have never used an AI tool; I would rather speak to the crew lead than have a program tell a resident a bin was emptied when it is still at the kerb.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the desk that AI Plateau may type a routine reply faster, but someone still has to ask a crew why a street was missed. I would not close a resident’s report merely because a route record says complete.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think our desk will keep its work if the software change is small. My partner’s kitchen wage is regular during term and we have four months saved, though the mortgage and school holiday weeks still need planning. I do not feel a need to start using AI for this.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep ringing the crew lead before closing any disputed route report and check the paper exception book at the end of the shift. If the mild software arrives next year, I would keep the same sign-off. I would continue our usual mortgage payments and put the school holiday dates on our household calendar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own job in this version. I get annoyed when an answer is sent before anyone has looked down the street.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does the exception book show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last month a crew marked Oak Lane complete because the large truck had passed the entrance. The small collection truck had not gone down the narrow lane. I rang the lead, and the bins were collected that afternoon.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try the draft reply tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not for a small saving. I have never used AI at work and would have to learn it from the beginning. My experienced desk staff can prepare a reply, but I want the crew record checked before it goes out.

say: A **routine reply** still needs a crew check before closure.
I would not trust a **completed route** mark without checking the street.
think: Our **missed-collection desk** looks steady under a mild change.
The **four-month reserve** helps, while holiday kitchen wages need planning.
do: **Keep** calling crew leads before closing disputed reports.
**Check** the exception book at the end of each shift.
**Continue** ordinary mortgage payments and plan for school holiday weeks.
feel: I feel **calm** about work but annoyed by replies sent before a street check.
S0.quote: The small collection truck had not gone down the narrow lane.
fieldNote: His **never-used-AI** stance is explicit; his knowledge comes from years on collection routes.
Four months saved and **term-time kitchen pay** make school holidays a planning issue, not a crisis.

steps.text: Call crew lead before closing disputed route reports
Check paper exception book at shift end
Continue mortgage payments and mark school holiday weeks on calendar

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say strong automation may answer residents and plan routes faster, and the company may cut desk jobs. I would ask the union to publish missed collections beside any claimed savings. The street and the worker should both count.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I know my practical route memory is good, but I am a new and weaker desk manager. Headquarters might combine complaint offices and make me compete for my post. Four months saved gives me some time, not years, and I cannot easily replace this wage locally.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would give the union branch ten cases where the completed-route record was wrong. I would ask the operations director for a paid morning with the route supervisor to learn the new exception screen, but attend only if the director approves desk cover and the supervisor has time to train me. If offices combine, I would apply for posted municipal-service coordinator work only with verified take-home pay that covers our mortgage and travel; I would accept only a confirmed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a combined office. I would be angrier if the company called a missed collection a successful efficiency gain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why ten cases?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten is enough for the branch to see whether the same narrow street keeps vanishing from the route record. I have the resident reports and crew notes for each one. One missed collection can be dismissed as a driver having a bad day.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move back onto a truck?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not without checking the actual vacancy, pay and physical requirements. I have been off a collection crew for years. A shorter desk course does not make me fit for a long lifting shift.

say: **Route automation** may cut desk posts while missed collections remain.
I would put **street failures** into union evidence.
think: My **new manager post** could be at risk in an office merger.
Four months saved gives time, but **local wage options** are limited.
do: **Give** the union ten documented false-complete routes next month.
**Request** a paid exception-screen morning; attend only with director-approved desk cover and supervisor training.
**Apply** for posted service-coordinator work only with mortgage-covering take-home pay after travel.
feel: I feel **anxious** about merger risk and angry at false efficiency claims.
S1.quote: One missed collection can be dismissed as a driver having a bad day.
fieldNote: He uses **ten route cases** for union evidence rather than assuming his memory alone proves a pattern.
His **screen learning** depends on paid time, approved desk cover and an available supervisor.

steps.text: Give union ten false-complete routes with resident and crew records
Attend paid exception-screen training only with approved desk cover and supervisor instruction
Apply to posted service roles only with mortgage-covering net pay after travel
Accept only confirmed offer with checked pay and duties

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues AGI by 2028 could answer complaints and make routes before anyone has agreed what happens to desk workers. I would ask the union for written notice and a named person who can reopen a false completed report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think our missed-collection desk may lose most of its posts, including mine. Other service coordinators also write and schedule, so 2028 AGI reaches them too. Crews still collect bins physically until robots around 2031, but I have no guaranteed crew vacancy and do not know whether I can manage the lifting at sixty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask the union branch to seek written severance and a resident-appeal rule. I would check our four-month savings against the mortgage and holiday kitchen-pay calendar with my partner. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I am cut, I would apply for advertised local service or depot work only with net pay after travel that covers our bills and duties I can physically perform; I would accept only a real offer with those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect the desk to shrink before I can learn another kind of work. Four months gives us a search, but it does not make the mortgage disappear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the kitchen wage alone carry you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. My partner’s school kitchen pay helps, but it does not pay the mortgage and bills alone, and holiday weeks can be shorter. I would not ask our grown children to put their wages into our plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should a resident appeal do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The resident should be able to show a photograph of a full bin and get a person to contact the crew. A digital completed stamp cannot empty a bin left at the kerb. The person answering must be able to reopen the route record.

say: **2028 AGI** could remove desk work before there is a fair plan.
I would demand **notice and appeals** for workers and residents.
think: My **own junior post** may go with most of the collection desk.
Service scheduling faces **2028 AGI**, while physical collection robots follow around 2031.
do: **Ask** union branch this week for severance and resident-appeal rules.
**Check** savings against mortgage and holiday kitchen wages with my partner.
**Apply** after a 2028 cut only for advertised work with bill-covering net pay and physically manageable duties.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about expected desk losses despite four months saved.
S2.quote: A digital completed stamp cannot empty a bin left at the kerb.
fieldNote: He expects **most desk posts** to vanish, including possible loss of his own junior role.
The **four-month reserve** funds a search, while crew jobs require verified pay, availability and physical fit.

steps.text: Ask union for written severance and resident-appeal rule
Apply after cut only to advertised work with bill-covering net pay and manageable physical duties
Accept only actual offer after checking pay after travel and physical tasks

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives the company time to train a real route checker and to agree that the union can inspect the error figures. I would want learning on a street with a crew, not only a screen demonstration.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I might manage a route-audit job if somebody patiently shows me the new reports and the actual street work. The audit paperwork still faces 2031 AGI, and the crews face capable robots around 2034. At 63 I cannot assume the physical part will suit me, or that retirement income will cover our bills without checking a statement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2027 I would request one paid route walk each month with the crew trainer; I would attend only if my desk manager approves cover and the trainer supervises the walk. I would ask payroll for the actual retirement-income statement and compare its conditions with our bills, without choosing a retirement date yet. After 2031 I would apply only for a posted route-audit role with verified wage after travel, real authority to correct records and walking duties I can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about becoming useful just as the paperwork changes. A paid walk would tell me more than an optimistic training leaflet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the trainer show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Which vehicle fits a narrow lane, when a crew can safely reverse and how to record a blocked entrance. I know the old routes from years ago. I need the crew trainer to show me the current collection vehicles before I sign a route audit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if a route-audit job is advertised?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would read the pay and walking duties before applying. A title does not say how far I must walk or whether I can correct a false completed mark. If those conditions are not stated, I would ask rather than assume.

say: **Five years** should fund real route checks and union access to error figures.
I would seek **street training** with a crew rather than a demonstration.
think: Route-audit paperwork faces **2031 AGI**, and physical collection robots follow around 2034.
At **63**, walking capacity and retirement income remain unverified.
do: **Request** a paid monthly crew walk in 2027; attend only with desk cover and trainer supervision.
**Request** actual retirement-income terms from payroll before setting any retirement date.
**Apply** after 2031 only for posted audit work with net pay, correction authority and manageable walking.
feel: I feel **anxious** about paperwork change but willing to test a supervised walk.
S3.quote: I need the crew trainer to show me the current collection vehicles before I sign a route audit.
fieldNote: His **route walk** is conditional on paid time, desk cover and current-vehicle supervision.
A **posted audit role** must have real correction authority, viable wages and manageable walking.

steps.text: Attend paid monthly route walks only with approved desk cover and crew-trainer supervision
Apply after 2031 for posted route audit only with viable pay, correction authority and manageable walking

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the union a decade allows written notice, human appeals and paid training for older workers. The company should show the cost of keeping a person who can correct a route, not only the saving from removing desk posts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I will be 68 in 2036. I might want to stop, but I have not verified any retirement income or eligibility, and four months saved alone will not pay indefinitely. Complaints and route audits face 2036 AGI; physical collection meets robots around 2039. A decade gives planning time, not a guaranteed pension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep checking crew notes and request an actual retirement-income statement, then compare verified income and savings with our bills. I would add forty to savings only in months when both wages arrive, the mortgage and utilities are paid and no school-holiday shortfall remains. After 2036 I would keep paid work if the job is real and retirement income plus savings cannot cover our bills; otherwise I would stop only after we check the numbers together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about being sixty-eight without a clear figure. I can plan the household, but I cannot call retirement secure yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the statement is lower than expected?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep seeking paid work and ask the union about actual notice and training rights. Our grown children have their own bills. I would not turn my grown children’s kindness into a monthly figure in our budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why save only forty?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The school kitchen roster shortens during holidays, and our mortgage still comes each month. Forty from a full-pay month is possible without touching our four-month reserve. If that roster is short, the extra transfer waits.

say: A **decade** should bring written notice, appeals and paid learning.
I would show the cost of **human route correction** beside staff savings.
think: At **68**, retirement income and eligibility remain unknown.
Desk work faces **2036 AGI**, with physical collection robots around 2039.
do: **Save** forty extra only after both wages, mortgage and utilities clear with no holiday-pay shortfall.
**Continue** paid work after 2036 if retirement income plus savings cannot cover bills.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about unverified retirement income despite planning time.
S4.quote: I would not turn my grown children’s kindness into a monthly figure in our budget.
fieldNote: He treats **retirement entitlement** as unverified and grown children’s help as uncertain.
His **extra saving** depends on both wages and no school-holiday pay gap, preserving the four-month reserve.

steps.text: Keep checking crew notes before closing route complaints
Save forty only with both wages mortgage utilities paid and no holiday-pay shortfall
Continue paid work after 2036 if verified retirement income plus savings cannot cover bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. The company could close most of the desk before I have a suitable new job, and four months saved will go. Written notice, a person who can reopen a route and paid supervised training would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask a crew lead whether the truck actually entered the lane. I have learned that a completed box on a form can be wrong. I do not want residents or waste crews told to trust an unchecked route-completion mark.

headlineQuote: I do not want residents or waste crews told to trust an unchecked route-completion mark.
portrait: **Emeka, 58**, is a junior missed-collection desk manager, new to staff budgets after years on waste routes.
His **typical pay**, school-kitchen partner, four-month reserve and some nearby jobs support a small mortgage.
He has **never used AI** and checks disputed records with actual crews.
He is **calm** under mild change, alarmed by rapid desk loss and cautious about retirement without verified terms.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his junior desk role before a suitable paid alternative is clear.
whatWouldHelp: Written **notice**, reopened resident appeals and paid supervised route learning would help.
